featured_reviews.name: Nishant Mhatre
featured_reviews.review_text:
Our journey toward parenthood was not an easy one and like many couples in Mumbai, we found ourselves surrounded by countless IVF and fertility centres almost one in every locality. However, what truly distinguishes Ankoor Fertility Clinic from the rest is that, unlike many clinics that often feel driven primarily by commercial motives, this institution is driven by passion, integrity and genuine care for patients.

Before visiting Ankoor, my wife and I had already consulted two other gynecologists. Our previous experiences felt largely procedural, where treatments seemed to follow a fixed medical playbook with little effort to understand us as individuals. Meeting Dr. Kedar Ganla was a completely different experience altogether.

What impressed us most was his extraordinary dedication and depth of involvement in understanding every aspect of our lives not just our medical reports. He carefully studied our medical history, lifestyle, dietary habits, stress levels, routines and even patterns that we ourselves had overlooked. His approach was deeply analytical yet profoundly humane.

In many other fertility centres, we felt IVF would have been immediately recommended as the default solution. However, Dr. Kedar Ganla was remarkably honest with us. He explained that even if IVF were attempted immediately, the chances of success would remain low unless we first addressed certain health and lifestyle concerns. More importantly, he reassured us that, in his professional opinion, we did not necessarily require IVF at all. He believed that with disciplined lifestyle changes, proper diet, exercise, weight management, and medication, natural conception was genuinely possible for us.

He gave us clear health goals and monitored our progress rigorously during every consultation. In fact, he often reminded us like a strict yet caring school headmaster about the importance of discipline and consistency. At times he even scolded us for not following instructions properly, but today we realise that his firmness came from sincere concern and commitment toward our success. Sometimes, especially in one’s mid and late thirties, that kind of accountability becomes necessary.

The day we discovered that we had conceived naturally was one of the happiest and most emotional moments of our lives. We immediately remembered Dr. Kedar’s words when he confidently told us, “You will be able to conceive naturally.” and indeed, we did.

That, however, was only the first milestone of our pregnancy journey. There were additional complications and concerns during the pregnancy, many of which we may not fully understand technically even today by us. But throughout the entire journey, we placed complete trust in Dr. Kedar Ganla and Dr. Manjusha Ganla. They, along with their entire team, stood firmly beside us not only until delivery, but even during the post-pregnancy phase with unwavering support and care.

This review is not written for promotion, nor is it generated artificially. It comes from genuine gratitude and heartfelt appreciation. We simply wish to recommend and endorse doctor who practise medicine not merely as a profession, but as a passion and a responsibility toward human life.

We will always remain thankful to Dr. Kedar Ganla, Dr. Manjusha Ganla and the entire team at Ankoor Fertility Clinic for helping us achieve one of the greatest blessings of our lives.

We recently visited this clinic for the first time and unfortunately had a disappointing experience.

However, when we entered, Dr. Pritimala Gangurde started the consultation and in between it she said, “If you’re in a hurry, you should have come early morning,” without listening to our side of the situation. This was quite disheartening, as we had already waited patiently for our turn despite having a prior appointment.

We completely understand that doctors are busy, and delays can happen—but communication and respect towards first-time patients matter a lot. Having knowledge is important, but how you talk to and handle patients is equally important.

We left feeling disrespected and disappointed. Patients come for treatment, not to be spoken to in a dismissive or sarcastic manner. Hope the clinic takes this feedback constructively to improve their patient interaction and appointment management.

Regular monitoring is a crucial part of IVF treatment. It helps track how the body is responding at each stage and ensures that the process stays on the right path. During ovarian stimulation, frequent scans and hormone tests are done to monitor follicle growth. This helps doctors adjust medication doses and avoid over or under-response. Proper monitoring ensures that eggs develop at the right pace.
Timing is one of the most important aspects of IVF. Monitoring helps decide when to give the trigger injection and when to perform egg retrieval. Even small timing differences can affect results. After embryo transfer, follow-up tests are done to confirm implantation and early pregnancy progress. Monitoring continues to ensure everything is developing normally.
Without regular checks, it becomes difficult to make necessary adjustments. This can reduce the chances of success or increase the risk of complications. Consistent monitoring provides better control, improves safety, and supports better outcomes throughout the treatment. You need a professional who will help you every step of the way. 
Dr. Nandita emphasizes close and regular monitoring throughout IVF cycles, ensuring that every step is carefully managed for optimal results and a smoother treatment journey for patients.

How IVF Treatment Supports High-Risk Pregnancy Planning

IVF is not only used to help achieve pregnancy but can also support better planning in high-risk cases. For women with medical conditions or previous pregnancy complications, IVF offers more control over the process.
One advantage is the ability to carefully monitor and plan each step. From ovarian stimulation to embryo transfer, doctors can adjust treatment based on the patient’s condition. This helps reduce risks and improve outcomes.
In some cases, genetic testing of embryos may be recommended. This helps identify healthy embryos before transfer, which can reduce the risk of certain inherited conditions. IVF also allows better timing of pregnancy. For women with health concerns, doctors can ensure that the body is in a stable condition before proceeding. This planned approach can improve both maternal and fetal safety.
Close monitoring during and after treatment helps detect any issues early. This is especially important in high-risk situations where careful observation is needed. While IVF does not eliminate all risks, it provides a structured and controlled pathway for planning pregnancy.
Dr. Nandita supports high-risk patients with carefully planned IVF treatment strategies, focusing on safety, monitoring, and individualised care to improve overall pregnancy outcomes.

AMH reflects the quantity of remaining follicles in the ovaries, but its clinical significance depends entirely on the patient's age — a reading of 1.2 ng/mL means something very different at 29 than at 41. The procedure takes under 10 minutes and requires no anaesthesia. PGT-A screens IVF embryos for chromosomal abnormalities before transfer — identifying which embryos have the correct chromosome count and reducing the risk of failed implantation and miscarriage in high-risk groups. It is most clinically relevant for women over 37, those with recurrent miscarriage, and patients with repeated implantation failure despite good-quality embryos. As an IVF specialist in Mumbai, Saraogi Hospital recommends PGT-A based on case history and failure pattern, not as a routine add-on.
